# loading libraries

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

```
# import data

```{r}
hg<-read.csv("gsssubset.csv")
head(hg)
```

# one way Anova
## test whether there are significance differences btn group means

```{r}
data7<-data.frame(
  group=factor(c("A","A","A","B","B","B","C","C","C")),
  value=c(5:13)
)
head(data7)
```



# perform 1 way ANOVA

## HO: there is no significance diffrence across the scores across the three groups
## H1: there is significance  scores across the three groups
```{r}
one_anova<-aov(value~group, data=data7)
summary(one_anova)
```

# results
- since the p-value<5%, we reject null hypothesis and conclude that exist significance btn the 3 groups


# post-hoc test(turkey's hsd) :  identify  which group differ significantly  after a significant anova results

```{r}
turkey_results=TukeyHSD(one_anova)
print(turkey_results)

```

- b-a exist



# plot the results

```{r}

plot(turkey_results)
```



# 2-way Anova
```{r}
data9<-data.frame(
 factor1=factor(c("X","X","X","Y","Y","Y")),
   factor2=factor(c("P","Q","R","P","Q","R")),
 value1=c(5:10)
)
head(data9)
```




# perform 2 way anova

## H0: there is no significance difference on avarage income across factor 1
## H1: there is no significance difference on avarage income across factor 2
## H2: there is no significance difference on avarage income across the interaction

```{r}
anova_model1<-lm(value1~factor1*factor2, data=data9)
anova_result<-anova(anova_model1)
print(anova_result)
```


# using real data set


## H0: there is no significance difference on avarage income across gender
## H1: there is no significance difference on avarage income across marital status
## H2: there is no significance difference on avarage income across the interaction



```{r}
hg$marital<-as.factor(hg$marital)
hg$sex<-as.factor(hg$sex)
anova_model_data<-lm(income~sex*marital, data=hg)
anova_tway<-anova(anova_model_data)
print(anova_tway)
```


- the data is significance 



# by degree

## H0: there is no significance difference on avarage income across degree
## H1: there is no significance difference on avarage income across marital status
## H2: there is no significance difference on avarage income across the interaction


```{r}
hg$marital<-as.factor(hg$marital)
hg$degree<-as.factor(hg$degree)
anova_model_data4<-lm(income~degree*marital, data=hg)
anova_tway2<-anova(anova_model_data4)
print(anova_tway2)
```

- degree ~marital,no significancy
income~degree * marital, significancy interaction exists


# non - parametric sets

## wilcoxon rank_sum test(mann-whitney u test): compare medians of 2 independent


```{r}
group00<-c(5:7)
group000<-c(8:10)
wilcon<-wilcox.test(group00, group000)
print(wilcon)
```

- since the p-value>5%, we fail to reject null analysis and conclude that their is no difference significant  btn median of  group (00 and 000)





# kruskal-wallis test: compare median of more than one group

## H0: median value of A=B=C
## H1: median value of A!=B!=C

```{r}
data222<-data.frame(
  group6=factor(c("A","A","A","B","B","B","C","C","C")),
  value=c(5:13)
)
head(data222)
```



# kruskal-willis test

```{r}
kruskal_results<-kruskal.test(value~group6, data=data222)
print(kruskal_results)
```


- sinjce p-value< 5%, we fail to reject the null hypontesis and conclude that there is a signifacnce difference in median btn group A, B and C



# using gsssubset

```{r}
kruskal_result2<-kruskal.test(hg$income~hg$marital, data=data222)
print(kruskal_result2)
```

- p-value<5%, we fail to reject,
